title: The Bioreactor Bid
primary_metric: liters of viable product yielded per dollar of vessel cost

options.A: The Column Bid — a standard cylindrical stirred-tank bioreactor
options.B: The Wave Bid — a wave/rocking bioreactor whose curved bag profile requires a disk-method volume calculation

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: No public per-vessel validation-cost benchmark exists for a 50 L single-use stirred-tank system; the named industry benchmark (BioPlan Associates [S6]) tracks this cost category but its dollar tables are subscription-gated. MA1 is a documented good-faith estimate, not a citation, so raising it far enough (+50%, to $22,500) can tie the two options at the infeasible-both floor rather than change which vessel a Hero should prefer.

The client's contractual minimum total yield is a fictional, program-specific contract term; no amount of research could reveal a real client's actual number, so it is set (25 L) to sit between the two vessels' working volumes and is the case's single most load-bearing, genuinely unknowable dial -- this is the intended, disclosed mechanism, not an accidental instability.

The CRO's program budget cap is a fictional, program-specific figure; it cannot be researched because no real program's internal budget ceiling for this scenario exists publicly. Set well above both totals so it is not binding at the stated value, but a large enough cut (-50%, to $25,000) eliminates the Column Bid too, producing a tie at infeasible-both rather than a flip to the Wave Bid.

Proxy for MA7 (Appendix C's bag radius profile): no manufacturer publishes a cross-sectional radius-vs-height profile for a rocking-motion bag -- Sartorius's own datasheet [S3] gives only bag volume sizes, and custom bag geometry is stated as engineered-to-order (proprietary). The profile is a documented, physically plausible good-faith estimate, and it is explicitly named in FACILITATOR.md and case.md's MA7 row as the single most load-bearing assumption in the case -- a flatter or taller profile changing the recommendation is the intended finding, not a defect.

Proxy for MA6 (Appendix A's feed-rate/uptake-rate table and the 0.05 L/g conversion factor): real published CHO fed-batch metabolic data exists only in cell-count- or cell-volume-normalized units, not g/L/day, so reaching this case's needed units would require additional unsourced conversions. The table is a documented good-faith estimate shaped like real Monod-kinetics data; case.md's own MA6 sensitivity note already discloses that its absolute scale determines whether the MA4 yield floor binds at all.

overview_numerals_cleared.why: incubator ambient temperature in degrees (Overview, 'hums at 37 degrees') -- atmosphere/texture only, not a clock time or year, never used in any D1-D5 calculation or appendix figure

cohort_bands.note: Anchors 2-4 run as written; the room should split on the primary-metric ratio (Wave ~12% ahead on yield-per-dollar) well before Anchor 4 surfaces the 25 L client-minimum constraint that disqualifies Wave outright -- expect a visible swing in the vote once that hard floor lands, since it is a disqualification, not a tiebreaker.

Anchors 2-3 combine into one pass; D1's area-between-curves arithmetic is worked once as a shared example (it is identical for both vessels), then pairs split to compute D2's two working-volume figures (cylinder for A, disk-method integral for B) and complete D3-D5 independently.

No vote to take -- Anchor 1 becomes a stated initial position instead of a cold-call; guide plays devil's advocate directly, pushing whichever side of the ratio-vs-floor tension the Hero under-weighted (a Hero who leads with the yield-per-dollar ratio gets pressed on the 25 L minimum; a Hero who leads with the floor gets pressed on how close the ratio actually is).

deliverables.text: A net-cumulative-yield calculation for the batch — the area between the feed-rate curve and the uptake-rate curve from Appendix A, in liters of viable product per liter of working volume, with your work shown.

A working-volume calculation for each vessel at the target fill level: for the Column Bid, the cylinder-volume formula applied to Appendix B's dimensions; for the Wave Bid, the disk-method integral of the bag's cross-sectional profile from Appendix C, including a labeled diagram of the solid of revolution you integrated.
A total-yield table showing liters of viable product for each vessel option (D1's per-liter net yield multiplied by each vessel's D2 working volume).
A yield-per-dollar comparison: liters of viable product yielded per dollar of total vessel cost (vessel plus validation, from Appendices B, C, and D), for both options.
An original visual display of the feed-rate and uptake-rate curves from Appendix A, with the area you used in D1 shaded and labeled.

balance.argument_a: The Column Bid's working volume (37.5 L, an exact cylinder-volume calculation at the 75% fill level) comfortably clears the client's 25 L contractual minimum yield [MA4], and its total cost ($43,864) sits well under the $50,000 program budget [MA5]. The Wave Bid, despite posting a higher yield-per-dollar ratio, only reaches 17.29 L of working volume once the disk-method integral is applied to its curved bag profile -- short of the 25 L floor by nearly a third. That floor is a hard constraint, not a tiebreaker: it disqualifies the Wave Bid outright regardless of how favorable its ratio looks, leaving the Column Bid as the only vessel that satisfies all three limits (yield floor, fill level, budget) at once.
balance.argument_b: On the metric Wei was actually asked to optimize -- liters of viable product yielded per dollar of total vessel cost -- the Wave Bid beats the Column Bid by about 12.4%: 17.29 L / $18,000 (~$0.00096/L-equivalent) versus the Column Bid's 37.5 L / $43,864 (~$0.00086/L-equivalent). The two vessels share the exact same net-cumulative-yield curve (Appendix A's feed-rate/uptake-rate table applies per liter of working volume to either vessel identically -- MA6), so this edge comes entirely from the Wave Bid's dramatically lower total cost ($18,000 vs. $43,864), not from any mixing-driven yield-per-liter advantage. A Hero could argue that the 25 L client minimum [MA4] is itself an unsourced modeling assumption rather than a physical limit, and that if it is negotiable -- or if this run is one of several batches counting toward a larger cumulative delivery -- the Wave Bid's clear cost-efficiency edge should carry the recommendation instead of a single run's yield floor.
balance.margin_basis: Compare total liters of viable product yielded per dollar of total vessel cost (net cumulative yield per liter, from the area between Appendix A's feed-rate and uptake-rate curves, times each vessel's working volume -- cylinder formula for the Column Bid, disk-method integral of Appendix C's bag profile for the Wave Bid -- divided by vessel-plus-validation cost from Appendices B, C, and D). Column: 37.5 L / $43,864 = 0.0008551 L/$. Wave: 17.29 L / $18,000 = 0.0009606 L/$. Wave leads on the raw ratio by (0.0009606-0.0008551)/0.0008551 = 12.36% (~12.4%), well inside the SPEC Section 2 ~20% cap -- a genuinely close, defensible race on the primary metric. The case's real dilemma is that the ratio-winner (Wave) fails the hard MA4 yield floor (17.29 L < 25 L) and is disqualified, so the Column Bid is the only feasible recommendation despite trailing on yield per dollar.

modeling_assumptions.basis: No public per-vessel validation-cost benchmark exists for a 50 L single-use stirred-tank system; the named industry benchmark (BioPlan Associates [S6]) tracks this trend but its dollar tables are subscription-gated.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Total Column cost is $43,864 vs. Wave's $18,000; yield/$ favors Wave by ~12%. Raising MA1 does not flip the recommendation on its own, since the yield floor (MA4) already decides it.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Single-use bag systems reportedly reduce CIP/SIP validation burden vs. reusable stirred tanks (qualitative, [S8]), but no quantitative benchmark is public.
Forced by Appendix A's existing table (6 rows, days 0-5). Real fed-batch mAb runs are typically 10-14 days [S7]; 5 days is a deliberately compressed pedagogical timeline.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Does not change the dilemma directly -- only bounds Appendix A's domain.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Client's minimum total viable product yield
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public source for a specific client's contractual minimum. Set between the two vessels' computed working-volume yields (Column 37.5 L, Wave 17.29 L) so the constraint is genuinely load-bearing.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Flips the case: Wave wins on yield-per-dollar (~$1,041/L vs. Column's ~$1,169/L, an ~12.4% margin) but fails a 25 L floor outright, so Column becomes the only feasible recommendation. Below ~17.3 L both options clear the floor and Wave wins outright; above ~37.5 L neither clears it.

modeling_assumptions.basis: No public source for a specific program's capex/validation ceiling. Set comfortably above both options' total costs ($43,864 Column, $18,000 Wave).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Not binding at this value. Below ~$43,864 it would eliminate the Column Bid regardless of the yield floor.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Appendix A feed-rate/uptake-rate table (12 values, days 0-5) and product-mass-to-volume conversion factor (0.05 L/g)
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public day-by-day g/L/day feed/uptake dataset exists for this (unnamed) cell line. Published CHO fed-batch metabolic data exists only in cell-count- or cell-volume-normalized units, which would require additional unsourced conversions. The case authors a table shaped like the qualitative pattern of real Monod-style kinetics.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Multiplies both vessels' totals identically, so it does not flip A vs. B by itself, but its absolute scale determines whether the MA4 yield floor binds at all.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Appendix C bag radius profile r(h) (5 height/radius pairs)
modeling_assumptions.basis: No manufacturer publishes a bag cross-sectional radius-vs-height profile for a rocking-motion bag; Sartorius's Flexsafe RM datasheet [S3] gives only bag volume sizes, and custom bag geometry is 'engineered to order' (proprietary). The case authors a physically plausible increasing-bulge profile.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly sets Wave's working volume (17.29 L via the disk-method integral) -- the load-bearing quantity for D2-D4 and the MA4 yield-floor check. A flatter or taller profile could push Wave's volume past 25 L and reopen the dilemma.
